title: Expression Trees
description: Understand expression trees and how they enable LINQ providers like Entity Framework.

data.text: An expression tree is an in-memory representation of a lambda expression arranged in a tree-like data structure. Each node in an expression tree is an expression.

Expression trees hold the actual elements of a query, not the result of the query. They make the structure of lambda expressions transparent and explicit, allowing you to interact with the data just like any other data structure.

data.title: Expression Tree Example
data.content: Creating an expression tree from a lambda
data.code: Expression<Func<Student, bool>> isTeenAgerExpr = s => s.Age > 12 && s.Age < 20;

data.title: Inspecting Expression Trees

data.text: Lambda expressions assigned to `Func<T>` compile into executable code for in-memory collections. Lambda expressions assigned to `Expression<TDelegate>` compile into expression trees.
Expression trees are essential for remote LINQ providers like LINQ-to-SQL and Entity Framework. They can be translated into SQL queries that execute on the database server.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Expression trees are in-memory representations of lambda expressions
They hold query structure, not results
Can be built manually using the Expression class
Enable LINQ providers to translate queries to SQL
